headline.purpose: One per view: the view title (h1).

title.purpose: Card headings, slider labels, question text, primary-button label, top-line values.

body.purpose: Running text; lede capped at 62ch in muted colour.

body-small.purpose: Fine print, legends, tables, axes, chips; the 16 px floor.

label.purpose: Uppercase marginalia for cell and section labels; never a kicker above an h1.

shadows.name: rail-current
shadows.purpose: Structural underline on the current rail item; the system's only box-shadow.

motion.name: none
motion.purpose: State changes are instant; prefers-reduced-motion also strips any browser-added transition or animation.

breakpoints.name: portrait-tablet
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: rail 104 px, top line wraps to two full rows, footer two columns.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: one column, rail on top, page scrolls, replay footer sticky.

sizes.name: hit-primary
sizes.purpose: Primary controls, slider tracks, rail items.

modes.mechanism: app/src/tokens.ts day and evening objects, written to :root custom properties by toCss() at runtime
modes.evening: 2700 K amber monochrome; blue channel at most 0.35 of max; advisory equals text amber

narrative.overview:
ANCHOR is a topographic survey sheet read at night. The ground is pine ink. The person's own normal is drawn on it as terrain: a moss corridor for the usual range, an ochre dashed benchmark for the pre-flight level, a lichen hinge where a consented new normal begins, and a cream trace for the person's own values. Everything else on the sheet, from the rail and top line to the controls, is ruled, flat and quiet so that the terrain and the reserved signal colours stay legible.

The system is an Operate shell for a tablet held at arm's length in a moving, dim cabin. That sets its density: few elements per screen, 19 px body type, 80 px minimum touch targets and 104 px primary ones. Labels are set in uppercase map-collar marginalia, figures are tabular with slashed zeros, and meaning never depends on colour alone. In the evening the whole sheet re-renders in a 2700 K amber monochrome, and shape and label take over everything that colour carried in the day.

The system rejects rings, gauges, composite scores and red/green status cards. Signal colours belong to NASA-STD-3001 meanings and nothing else.
keyCharacteristics: Flat, ruled panels on a single dark ground; depth comes from one tonal step and 1 px rules.
One accent (lichen) for selection and the primary action; signal colours reserved for their meaning.
Large, calm controls: 80 px minimum, 104 px primary, and drag-anywhere tracks.
Dashed strokes mark reference, not-yet or not-live states throughout.
Two complete token sets, day and evening, swapped at runtime on the same CSS custom properties.

rules.name: The Six-to-One Rule
rules.body: Every text and background pair is at least 6:1 in both day and evening modes, including disabled text. `app/test/tokens.test.ts` enforces this; a new text pairing must pass it before it ships.

rules.name: The 2700 K Rule
rules.body: No evening token may be bluer than a 2700 K source (blue channel at most 0.35 of the maximum channel). The evening set is amber monochrome; advisories rely on shape and label.

rules.name: The Reserved Signal Rule
rules.body: Warning red, caution yellow and advisory blue appear only for their NASA-STD-3001 meaning. They are never decoration, selection or brand.

rules.name: The Ochre-Is-Line Rule
rules.body: Contour ochre draws grid and benchmark lines only. It is never used as text or as a fill, and the token test fails if it is used as a text colour.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: `tabular-nums slashed-zero` is set on `:root`, so every figure has the same width (ten repeats of all ten digits measure 120.0 px at 19 px) and every zero is slashed. Do not switch it off for any number.

rules.name: The Map-Collar Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked text is used only for marginalia: a cell or section label in the label style. It never sits stacked above an h1 as a kicker, and a message card's register word stays inline on its heading line.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never lift. A panel is distinguished by its tone, its rule or its border weight, never by a shadow.

rules.name: The Dashed Edge Rule
rules.body: A dashed stroke means reference, not yet, or not live: the pre-flight benchmark, an unrated slider, a disabled control, the read-only note, the synthetic badge, loss of signal on the mission-day strip and an undone hinge. A solid stroke means the person's live state.

rules.name: The Shape-Carries-It Rule
rules.body: A register is carried by shape and word together, and colour only repeats it. This must survive the evening rendering, where advisory blue becomes amber.

dos: **Do** reference colours through the runtime custom properties (`var(--accent)`, `var(--line)`) so the evening set reaches every component.
**Do** keep every text pair at 6:1 or better in both modes, and run `app/test/tokens.test.ts` after any token change.
**Do** size touch targets at 80px minimum and 104px for the primary control on a screen.
**Do** carry every register with its glyph shape (diamond, triangle, circle, rule) and its word, and let colour only repeat them.
**Do** mark not-yet, reference and not-live states with a dashed stroke, and live state with a solid one.
**Do** keep figures tabular with slashed zeros, and keep text at 16px or larger.
**Do** size chart SVGs to the sheet width so one unit is one CSS px.
donts: **Don't** use warning red, caution yellow or advisory blue for anything but their NASA-STD-3001 meaning, and don't use blue at all in the evening set.
**Don't** use contour ochre for text or fills.
**Don't** fade disabled controls with opacity. Use muted text on the ground with a dashed border.
**Don't** add drop shadows or lift surfaces. Depth is one tonal step and a rule.
**Don't** introduce rings, gauges, composite scores or red/green status cards.
**Don't** stack an uppercase label above a heading as a kicker. Marginalia labels cells and sections only.
